judgments.forked_readings_summary:
All four read the SAME task: add a new read-only tools/preflight-export.sh (sibling to preflight-install.sh / preflight-verify.sh) that takes <CONSUMER_DIR>, reads that consumer's accumulated .preflight/ runtime state, and writes it to a single portable, provenance-stamped (HEAD/tag/timestamp) archive without mutating the repo, plus a behavioral test under tests/behavioral/. Core behavior is in full agreement, including the shared, explicit out-of-scope set: no import/restore, no upload/transport, no redaction/encryption, no web UI / accounts / DB, and the unanimous clarification that "their data" means per-run .preflight/ operational state, not application/customer data (no GDPR semantics — none of that exists in this repo).

The only divergences are detail-level, not task-level:
1) Archive CONTENTS breadth. #1 names a subset (decisions/, gate/, cache/derived-state.json, installed.lock). #3 and #4 say package the WHOLE .preflight/ tree (adding track-record/, migrate-checkpoint.json, adjudications/, config). #2 is in between but uniquely adds "the RESOLVED rubric" via lib/resolve-config.sh / rubric-resolve.sh so exported captures stay interpretable — the most expansive read, lightly touching a config-resolution helper, but still framed as read-only packaging. All real .preflight/ subtrees per defaults/preflight-gitignore; this is a completeness nuance of one deliverable, not a competing task.
2) Docs surface. Only #4 pulls CLAUDE.md (Commands) + FRAMEWORK.md (tools overview) into scope to honor single-source-of-truth; the other three don't mention docs. A minor extra surface named by one reading.
3) Test rigor. #3/#4 explicitly require wiring the test into tests/run-all-tests.sh; #1/#2 just say "behavioral test." Same intent, different specificity.

No reading would build something another would call the wrong task — they'd all ship a preflight-export.sh that bundles .preflight/ into a portable archive.

All four read the SAME task: add a new read-only tools/preflight-export.sh <CONSUMER_DIR> (sibling to preflight-install.sh/preflight-verify.sh) that bundles one consumer's accumulated .preflight/ run-state into a single portable, timestamped, manifest/provenance-stamped archive (HEAD SHA + framework tag + timestamp), reading existing files only and never mutating the repo, plus a new tests/behavioral/ test proving the archive is produced and well-formed. All four converge on the same out-of-scope set: no import/restore, no upload/transport, no redaction/anonymization, no web-UI / SaaS-account / customer-DB notion ("their data" = the framework's per-run .preflight/ state), and no hooks/gate changes. The only differences are non-forking detail variations: (1) which .preflight/ artifacts each engineer enumerates as archive contents — reading 1 lists the fewest (decisions/gate/cache/installed.lock), readings 3 and 4 list nearly the full tree (config, gate, adjudications, decisions, metrics, track-record, derived/cache, migration checkpoint, installed.lock), reading 2 sits between. These are partial enumerations of the same real directory (confirmed against defaults/preflight-gitignore, which defines exactly these artifacts under .preflight/), not different scopes. (2) Reading 2 alone pulls in the resolved rubric (outside .preflight/, via lib/resolve-config.sh) so captures stay interpretable. (3) Reading 4 alone adds documenting the tool in CLAUDE.md + FRAMEWORK.md per the single-source rule. Both are small, defensible elaborations of the same deliverable rather than a divergent task. Core deliverable (export tool + behavioral test) is identical across all four.

All four read the same task: add a new read-only tools/preflight-export.sh that reads a single consumer's accumulated .preflight/ runtime state (decisions, adjudications, gate evidence, cache/derived, metrics, config, installed.lock, etc. — drawn from the same tree the defaults/preflight-gitignore enumerates) and writes ONE portable, timestamped, provenance/manifest-stamped archive to local disk, failing closed when .preflight/ is absent, plus a tests/behavioral/ test wired into run-all-tests.sh. All four explicitly exclude the same things: no import/restore, no upload/transport, no redaction/encryption, no mutation of the repo, no UI/account/DB product, no SaaS/GDPR/user-data semantics, no installer/hook/gate changes.

Differences are detail-level, not scope forks: (1) exactly which .preflight/ sub-artifacts each enumerates varies (#1 names cache/derived-state.json; #4 adds migrate-checkpoint + track-record; #3 broadest; all are 'everything under .preflight/'). (2) #2 additionally bundles the resolved rubric (via lib/resolve-config.sh) so captures stay interpretable — an additive data-source detail. (3) #4 alone lists documentation surfaces (CLAUDE.md Commands section + FRAMEWORK.md tools overview) as in-scope deliverables; #1–#3 are silent on docs. An implementer following any of the four would build the same tool with the same boundary; the deltas are edge additions, not competing readings of the task.
